one_line: Privacy-preserving lost-and-found matching with agent-mediated ownership verification.
what_it_does: Lets finders list items with private details and lets claimants answer verification questions; the server returns only verified or not verified.
leverage_rationale: The agent is central to conducting a conversational ownership interview while keeping secret answers hidden; a generic UI-driving agent could attempt it but would have less reliable structured access and privacy guarantees.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies page-native tools for search, opening a match, and verification without exposing answers.
Frames show an agent/sidebar alongside the search and wallet verification flow.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent search-to-candidate-to-verification experience, but the frame evidence is low-resolution and does not show a completed verified outcome.
execution_evidence: Frames show item search form and a candidate Wallet Brown page with ownership questions.
Devpost screenshot shows the product packaging and verification concept, but the embedded video is paused.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete, high-friction trust problem in lost-and-found communities, especially where public disclosure can enable fraudulent claims.
impact_evidence: Pitch and story identify the specific privacy-versus-proof problem.
Verification returns only a binary result and never reveals private details.
creativity_rationale: Using an agent as a private verifier rather than merely a search assistant is a memorable and well-targeted interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Private ownership interview and non-disclosing verification are the core concept.
The page-scoped toolset changes as the agent moves through the flow.
usability_note: Guided item description and conversational verification appear approachable, though the supplied frames are too small to assess details.
red_flags: No completed verified result is visible in the supplied evidence.
Frame sheets are difficult to read.
standouts: Agent is meaningfully integrated into the trust workflow.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-impact use of WebMCP with coherent but incomplete visual evidence.

one_line: Agent proposes a weekly staff rota while a manager reviews and approves every change.
what_it_does: Builds and audits shift schedules, exposes rules, coverage, cost, and staged edits, and keeps commit authority with the human manager.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools, shared live schedule state, staged mutations, and explicit human approval make the agent materially safer and more precise than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Story describes read-only analysis plus staged assignments and no commit tool.
Devpost visual advertises 36 tools and no commit tool; frames show dense schedule/review states.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a highly intentional workflow with coverage, rule breaches, cost, approval, audit logging, and light/dark states; end-to-end commit behavior is not directly shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show a polished scheduling/table workflow and review/approval panels.
Description enumerates before/after coverage, breaches, cost, audit records, and export.
impact_rationale: Scheduling errors directly affect staffing, childcare, compliance, and wage cost; the proposed workflow credibly helps managers without removing accountability.
impact_evidence: Story identifies fourteen staff, weekly coverage, rest rules, and GBP budget constraints.
Human approval is designed around consequences of rota mistakes.
creativity_rationale: The consent-first agent proposal model and auditable staged edits are a fresh treatment of a familiar scheduling category.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes but cannot commit.
Every edit includes explicit approval consequences and caller/tool auditability.
usability_note: Coverage, breaches, cost, roster, and approval surfaces suggest strong operational usability.
red_flags: No playing video or direct end-to-end approval result in the screenshot evidence.
standouts: Strong operational detail and audit trail.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: clear WebMCP delta, consequential audience need, and unusually complete workflow design.

one_line: A shared planner for selecting self-hosted infrastructure profiles and checking declared capacity.
what_it_does: Lets users and agents select module-level compute profiles, assess CPU/RAM/storage declarations, and generate a read-only CLI handoff.
leverage_rationale: Native tools share validated planner state and produce structured capacity assessments and handoffs; UI automation could reproduce much of it but with more ambiguity and friction.
leverage_evidence: Four named read-only tools share the same human UI state.
Frames show module profile selection and increasingly detailed capacity controls.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent from kit choice through independent module profiles, capacity assessment, and handoff, with clear boundaries that nothing runs in-browser.
execution_evidence: Frames show a consistent module profile planner with selected cards, expanded settings, and capacity controls.
Description specifies below-minimum blocking, missing declarations remaining unverified, and Markdown/CLI outputs.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real pain point for self-hosting users who need honest resource planning and reproducible handoff, though the audience is specialized.
impact_evidence: Story targets self-hosted infrastructure planning and avoids agents guessing from prose.
Per-module capacity choices support constrained hosts.
creativity_rationale: Module-specific profiles and honest declared-capacity semantics are a thoughtful, focused angle on infrastructure planning.
creativity_evidence: Independent module profiles rather than one global tier.
Read-only agent handoff is deliberately bounded.
usability_note: Visible staged planner, transparent per-axis assessment, and copyable handoff favor practical use.
red_flags: Capacity is declared assessment, not actual host compatibility; evidence does not show final handoff output.
standouts: Clear safety boundary: no browser execution.
advance_reason: Strong, credible developer-tool workflow with a meaningful structured-state advantage.

one_line: A fashion and sewing school where agents guide learners through lessons, quizzes, reflections, and essays.
what_it_does: Combines course content, practical video lessons, layered assessments, authentication, persistent progress, and WebMCP tools for contextual guidance.
leverage_rationale: Shared learner progress and curriculum-aware tools can improve agent guidance, but a general agent with access to the visible course UI could achieve much of the same outcome.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five browser-native tools and signed-in learner state.
No frame sheets were submitted, so the actual tool interaction is unverified.
execution_rationale: The claimed scope is substantial and coherent, but there are no frame-sheet images and the packaging screenshot alone cannot establish that the central learning workflow completes.
execution_evidence: Description lists three learning paths and persistent assessments.
No video frame sheets submitted; Devpost packaging is not runtime proof.
impact_rationale: Adult and working learners in practical fashion education have a clear need for scalable, contextual guidance and assessment.
impact_evidence: Story identifies practical control points, exercises, and instructor-scaling limitations.
Course structure includes sewing and design paths with substantial ordered content.

creativity_evidence: Fashion/sewing curriculum combines demonstrations, quizzes, reflections, and essays.
Agent is positioned as contextual support rather than replacing learner work.
usability_note: The described progression is promising, but login and absent runtime frames leave usability unclear.
red_flags: No frame sheets or video evidence submitted.
Large claimed scope cannot be checked from packaging alone.
advance_reason: Potentially valuable, but evidence is too thin to support advancement at this stage.

one_line: A natural-language collaborative floor-plan simulator for inventing future living spaces.
what_it_does: Lets users and agents inspect, propose, validate, and apply structured floor-plan changes, then export the current layout.
leverage_rationale: Structured inspect/propose/validate/apply operations over shared floor-plan state are substantially more reliable than trying to manipulate a visual editor through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Story names the complete inspect/propose/validate/apply flow and structured room/wall/furniture data.
212-second video exists and frame sheets show multiple floor-plan interaction states.
execution_rationale: The packet communicates a coherent editing model and the frames provide substantial product-motion evidence, though the supplied analysis cannot confirm every export path.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets show floor-plan simulator states and iterative configuration.
Description specifies underlying structured data and PNG/PDF export.
impact_rationale: It lowers the barrier to spatial ideation for people who want to imagine unconventional homes without learning specialized CAD controls.
impact_evidence: Story explicitly targets natural-language accessibility for floor-plan design.
Future devices and living systems extend beyond conventional furniture planning.
creativity_rationale: The combination of natural-language floor-plan editing and invention of future living systems is highly memorable and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Concept centers on turning imagined ways of living into visible structured spaces.
Agent collaborates through proposal and validation rather than opaque generation.
usability_note: Natural-language edits plus visible validation and export suggest an approachable creative workflow.
red_flags: Agent invocation details are not fully legible in the frame evidence.
advance_reason: Ambitious, memorable creative product with strong visual and WebMCP evidence.

one_line: An agent-controlled tldraw canvas for creating and arranging diagrams and visual scenes.
what_it_does: Exposes structured canvas inspection, page, shape, layout, embed, and drawing operations so agents can create and refine visual compositions.
leverage_rationale: Canvas state and bounded object mutations are much more precise through structured tools than generic coordinate-based browser automation, especially when preserving existing work.
leverage_evidence: Description lists inspection, creation, editing, alignment, layering, and fit-to-view tools.
Frames show a rich visual canvas/tableau workflow rather than a single button action.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the described preserve-inspect-refine loop is intentional, but the packet does not show a clearly completed end-to-end composition in readable detail.
execution_evidence: Story describes pages, diagrams, Mermaid, embeds, images, and layout operations.
Frame sheets show repeated canvas/editor states.
impact_rationale: Designers, educators, and developers can benefit from rapidly producing diagrams and visual explanations through natural language.
impact_evidence: Use cases include welcome screens, scenes, diagrams, Mermaid, and visual refinement.
Agent is intended to preserve and improve user canvas work.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a live spatial canvas with iterative visual checking is a fresh and expressive interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent creates and corrects compositions instead of only generating text.
Broad canvas vocabulary supports mixed visual artifacts.
usability_note: Natural-language canvas control is compelling, though broad tool scope may require careful guardrails.
red_flags: Submission says the original repository existed since 2025, making the project origin pre-existing with WebMCP additions.
Exact final visual quality is hard to judge from low-resolution sheets.
standouts: Preservation of existing work is a valuable constraint.
advance_reason: High leverage and creativity with a credible, expressive agent-native canvas workflow.

leverage_evidence: Description lists eight tools for story context, current scenes, characters, continuity, and more.

execution_evidence: Story explains the blind-context problem and structured workspace solution.

impact_rationale: Screenwriters and directors have a real recurring problem of maintaining continuity and creative constraints across scenes and sessions.
impact_evidence: Story identifies copy-pasted context, character history, and contradiction problems.
Tools target live narrative context and director rules.
creativity_rationale: Treating the screenplay as a stateful multi-dimensional workspace with an agent assistant is a strong, domain-specific interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent reads structured story/character/scene state instead of relying on pasted prompts.
Human director retains acceptance authority.
usability_note: Contextual assistance and review states appear well matched to professional writing practice.
red_flags: No readable end-to-end accepted revision is demonstrated.
No transcript and low-resolution frame evidence limit confidence.
standouts: Excellent fit between domain pain and structured WebMCP state.
advance_reason: Compelling agent-native writing workflow with clear audience need and meaningful structured-context advantage.

one_line: An incident console whose agent permissions escalate with severity and require human approval.
what_it_does: Shows service health and SLOs, mounts read-only or dangerous tools according to incident severity, and requires a human to approve rollback-like actions.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic page-owned tool registration makes authorization a live incident state: the agent’s available capabilities change as severity changes, a distinction generic UI automation cannot reliably reproduce.
leverage_evidence: Story explicitly describes tools mounting at green/yellow/blue severity and destructive tools disappearing.
Frames show severity escalation, approval card, charts recovering, and a 10/10 strip.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a tightly coherent incident workflow with alerting, charts, escalation reasoning, approval, rollback, and post-action recovery; the exact live invocation is not directly shown.
execution_evidence: Description enumerates console, severity-specific tool tray, approval, and SLO recovery states.
Frame sheets visibly include green alert, escalation panel, approval card, and blue state with destructive tools gone.
impact_rationale: Production incident response is high-stakes work where faster diagnosis and constrained automation can materially reduce downtime without granting standing destructive access.
impact_evidence: Story identifies the concrete 3 a.m. on-call risk and dangerous rollback problem.
Human on-call retains approval while the agent handles read/diagnostic work.
creativity_rationale: Making the WebMCP tool surface itself an incident-severity permission boundary is an unusually strong and memorable use of the medium.
creativity_evidence: Tools appear and disappear with incident state.
Escalation must be argued for and destructive actions require approval.
usability_note: Severity, SLO, timeline, tool tray, and approval surfaces map well to on-call decision-making.
red_flags: The packet has no transcript and does not directly show a live agent call in the provided frames.
advance_reason: Outstanding leverage and creativity with a concrete high-stakes audience and strong staged evidence.
